Severe Flooding Disrupts Retail Industry Operations Across Java, Indonesia

JAKARTA, Indonesia, June 13 – Widespread flooding caused by days of torrential rain has inundated retail industry sites across central and eastern Java, forcing store closures, damaging inventory, and disrupting operations at distribution centers, industry officials said on Thursday.

Major retail chains and local outlets alike have been impacted as water levels rose in low-lying commercial districts in cities including Surabaya, Semarang, and Solo. The Indonesian Retailers Association (APRINDO) reported that at least 220 retail sites have experienced significant water damage, with dozens more at risk as rainfall continues.

“At our Surabaya distribution hub, more than 70 percent of stock has been affected by floodwater, including electronics, clothing, and packaged food,” said Eko Santoso, operations manager at Sinar Nusantara Retail. “We have shut down the site for safety, and our workers have been evacuated.”

Workers at retail stores and warehouses across the region described difficult conditions as floodwaters cut off access to their workplaces. “We are worried about our jobs. Many of us cannot come to work, and those who do are helping move goods to higher shelves,” said Nia Putri, a cashier at a Semarang department store.

APRINDO Secretary-General Ratna Widjaja warned that ongoing flooding may lead to further closures and could threaten retail employment in the affected areas. “The safety of our workers is the top priority. We are coordinating with local authorities to monitor the situation and provide support to affected employees,” she said.

Retail sites in shopping centers, standalone stores, and warehouse complexes have reported damage to storage areas, fixtures, and merchandise. Several retailers have begun relocating undamaged goods to upper floors or offsite storage, but persistent rainfall has hampered these efforts.

“Initial estimates suggest losses in the tens of billions of rupiah, and this figure may rise if the flooding continues,” said retail analyst Dedi Prabowo. “Recovery will depend on how quickly the waters recede and sites can be cleaned and repaired.”

With floodwaters yet to subside, industry officials urged retail workers and site managers across Java to prioritize safety and to follow emergency protocols as the situation develops.
